The river at Jia roughly flows from east to west. The right figure is the river cross-section at Jia mentioned in the question stem; the left side of the cross-section is marked “south,” and the right side is marked “north”; in the figure, “sediments” are concentrated on the left side, that is, the south bank, and the south-bank slope is gentler, while the right side, that is, the north-bank slope, is steeper, showing an erosion bank. Reasoning: The question stem confirms that the right figure is the river cross-section at Jia, so the river flow direction in the left figure can be matched with the south and north banks in the right figure. When the river flows from east to west, facing downstream, the right-hand side is the north bank. The right figure shows that the north bank is a steeper erosion bank, and the south bank is a deposition bank. Rivers in the Northern Hemisphere are affected by the geostrophic deflection force and deflect to the right, usually with right-bank erosion and left-bank deposition; in the Southern Hemisphere it is the opposite. Therefore the area shown in the figure is located in the Northern Hemisphere.
